eli5.text: The automated system that builds the service now runs a single command at the top level instead of two separate commands nested inside subdirectories. This fixes the build failures that were happening in the automation. Only the internal build process is affected, so nothing users would see directly changes.

ai.title: CI pipeline: move credentials step before build
ai.summary: The CI workflow now retrieves secrets and writes .env.local before the build step, ensuring environment variables are available during compilation. Dependency installation uses --frozen-lockfile to enforce deterministic builds. The credentials step was moved from post-build to pre-build in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

eli5.text: When the build process runs, it now fetches the secret configuration files before compiling anything, so they're ready to use during the build. This affects anyone who triggers or relies on the automated testing and deployment system. You wouldn't see anything on your screen, but the build is now more reliable because it can access needed settings earlier in the process.

ai.title: Integrate Nx build orchestration for npm-app and web
ai.summary: Nx replaces manual `bun run --filter` scripts for `build`, `clean`, and `typecheck-only` tasks across the monorepo. New `project.json` files for `npm-app` and `web` define explicit build targets, dependency graphs (`implicitDependencies`), and output caching. `npm-app` scripts now invoke `nx build`/`nx clean` and use `tsconfig-paths/register` for runtime path resolution. `web` moves `contentlayer` generation and `next build` into Nx targets with `dependsOn` constraints.

eli5.text: The build system that prepares the web app and the npm tool for release has been switched from a set of manual scripts to a single coordinating tool. Instead of separately running several build commands in different folders and copying files by hand, those steps are now defined in one place that understands the order and dependencies between tasks. What you'd notice: running build, clean, or typecheck now uses fewer commands and produces the same result faster because it only rebuilds what actually changed. This is live today across the main project files.

eli5.text: When you finish a task in the terminal, the tool stopped printing a redundant 'Command completed.' line, so the screen no longer fills with repeated status messages. Instead, it now adds subtle spacing and cleaner formatting so your next prompt reads more naturally. If you use the npm-app CLI, you’ll notice the output looks tidier and less cluttered after commands finish.

ai.title: Fix npm app tests
ai.summary: CI workflow updated to execute `bun test **.ts` for npm-app, backend, and common packages to ensure proper file discovery. `tool-renderers.ts` modified to return double newline (`\n\n`) instead of single newline after file list rendering. Changes confined to CI configuration and internal rendering logic.

eli5.text: The system's automated test suite now finds and runs every test file correctly by telling the test runner to look for TypeScript files explicitly, and file lists now display with a blank line separating them from following text. If you browse GitHub's continuous-integration checks you will see three test commands (for the npm app, backend, and common packages) that previously could skip some test files now include a file-pattern argument guaranteeing all matching tests are discovered. The rendering tweak means any on-screen list of tool outputs appears with one extra blank line after it rather than none. These fixes are internal and already live on the main branch.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.260
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.260 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release update.

eli5.text: The app's version number was ticked up to reflect a new bundle of recent fixes that already went live for users. Among those fixes, the background system that builds the app now runs a bit more directly, and the test suite that checks npm-related features now runs as part of the build so problems are caught sooner. If you updated to this version, nothing visually changed in the app itself; it just pulls in those already-released improvements, and the version label lets tools and services know they are working with the current release.

ai.title: CI test globs anchored to cwd
ai.summary: Test commands in ci.yml now use `bun test ./**.ts` instead of `bun test **.ts`. The unanchored glob could match files outside the target package directory, causing spurious failures or missed tests. Scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml. Detail: applies to npm-app, backend, and common jobs.

eli5.text: The automated checks that confirm code works before it ships now look at the correct folders each time. When the system ran its routine verification across the three main software sections, it previously could grab test files from nearby sections instead of sticking to the one it was actually checking, which sometimes made it report the wrong pass or fail results. You would not see any difference in the product itself, but these checks now run more reliably in the background.

ai.title: Add Nx cache troubleshooting docs
ai.summary: Added Troubleshooting section to README.md and Build System Notes to knowledge.md. Documents resolution for Nx SQLite cache corruption errors ('database disk image is malformed') caused by process termination or disk errors. Instructs users to run `bunx nx reset` or `npx nx reset` to clear cache and stop daemon, noting subsequent builds will be slower.

eli5.text: If your build breaks with a message about a corrupted database image, the project now has written instructions telling you to run a reset command to clear the cached build data, after which builds will run slower until they rebuild. The documentation was added to the project's main setup guide so anyone hitting this error knows how to get unstuck. Nothing about the build process itself changed, only the explanations for what to do when the cache fails.

eli5.text: Your AI assistant is now running a newly packaged version that was assembled today with a few quiet improvements tucked inside. Among other small polish items, the build system now pays closer attention to the folder you run it from when executing test commands, and a short troubleshooting guide was added to the main help document for users hitting cache-related warnings. If you open the assistant now, nothing visible looks different, but the package reports it is the freshest build labeled 1.0.261.

ai.title: CI test steps switch from inline cd to working-directory
ai.summary: CI test steps in .github/workflows/ci.yml replace inline `cd` commands with the `working-directory` parameter for npm-app, backend, and common packages. This ensures the retry action executes tests from the correct context without shell chaining issues. Scope limited to CI workflow configuration. The `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS` environment variable remains set per command.

eli5.text: The automated system that checks new code before it goes live used to shuffle between folders by typing a shortcut command directly into the testing instructions, which sometimes caused it to lose track of where it was. Now it tells the testing tool upfront which folder to work in, so each round of checks runs from the right place without getting confused. This only affects how the checking system itself behaves; nothing visible to you outside of that process changes.

ai.title: Add newlines to update messages
ai.summary: Prepends newline characters to console output in `update-codebuff.ts`. Improves readability by separating update success and restart instructions from preceding logs. Affects CLI update flow only.

eli5.text: When the assistant tells you that it updated itself and that you should restart it, those two messages no longer run together with earlier log lines; they now each start on their own blank line so they're easier to spot. Who this affects: people running the assistant from the command line when it updates itself. What you'd notice: if you watched the text scroll by during a self-update, the success message and the restart instruction appear with a little extra space above them, instead of being jammed up against the lines that came before.

ai.title: CI test glob patterns corrected
ai.summary: CI test commands updated to use explicit `**/*.test.ts` globs instead of `./*.ts` with `working-directory` context. This ensures `bun test` correctly targets test files in `npm-app`, `backend`, and `common` within the GitHub Actions runner. Scope limited to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: If the automated test suite for the company's internal code was run, it might have wrongly skipped or failed on test files located in subdirectories of the npm-app, backend, and common folders. The fix makes the test-running instructions look specifically for files ending in.test.ts inside those subdirectories, instead of all.ts files at the top level. This prevents the build check from incorrectly passing when tests in those subdirectories aren't actually being executed.

ai.title: CI pipeline split into parallel jobs with dependency caching
ai.summary: The single `build-and-test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was decomposed into a `setup` job and four parallel downstream jobs (`build`, `typecheck`, `test-npm-app`, `test-backend`, `test-common`). The `setup` job now handles checkout, Bun installation, and credential generation, then caches `node_modules` using `actions/cache@v3` keyed by `bun.lockb`. Subsequent jobs restore this cache to avoid redundant installs. Working directory configurations were removed from test steps, relying on global paths instead.

eli5.text: When your code changes get submitted, the system that checks everything works now runs faster by doing several jobs at the same time instead of one long sequence. The process first prepares everything needed and remembers what it already downloaded, so the later checks don't waste time downloading the same things again. The backend and common test groups now share one computer each while the npm app gets its own, and they all start as soon as the step before them finishes. You won't see this directly unless you're waiting on a pull request to clear checks, but approvals should come through sooner.

eli5.text: If you looked at the project's automated checking process, you might notice it now passes along a file containing private settings between its separate checking steps, instead of assuming that file would still be sitting around from a previous step. This file holds the credentials needed for the checks to connect to external services, and now each checking step reliably retrieves a fresh copy rather than depending on leftover workspace data.

This replaces the previous mechanism of passing the flag via inline command env vars and sharing `.env.local` across jobs using `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact`. eli5.text: The automated system that checks the project for problems now writes its special settings file directly inside each step instead of passing it around between steps as a shared package. This makes the checking process more reliable and stops it from depending on a specific version of the build tool that could change unexpectedly. If you were watching the checks run, you'd see fewer steps related to uploading and downloading that settings file between stages.

ai.title: CI build and typecheck merged into single job

eli5.text: The system stopped running two separate checks on every code change and now runs them as one step instead. If you looked, you would see one fewer status check reporting in for each change. This only affects people working on the codebase itself, not what you see when using the app.

ai.title: CLI auto-detects git root and passes cwd to agent
ai.summary: The CLI now automatically resolves the project root by scanning parent directories for `.git` if no path is explicitly provided, ensuring consistent context regardless of the current working directory. The resolved `cwd` is added to the `ClientAction` schema and injected into the system prompt via `asSystemMessage`, allowing the agent to accurately track its location. This change affects `npm-app/src/index.ts`, `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, and `common/src/actions.ts`, with `findGitRoot` implemented in `npm-app/src/utils/git.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run the tool from inside a subfolder, it now figures out which project you're working on by looking for your project's hidden folder marker, instead of getting confused when you're not at the top level. The tool will also know exactly which folder it's supposed to be working in, so it keeps better track of where you are. This means it works reliably no matter which folder you launched it from within your project.

ai.title: Add calculate-monthly-usage script
ai.summary: Added scripts/calculate-monthly-usage.ts to compute monthly credit usage. Queries schema.message for total credits, user count, and message count within a YYYY-MM range. Also retrieves top 10 users by credit consumption. Defaults to 2025-04 if no argument provided.

eli5.text: The company has added an internal tool that lets staff pull a monthly report showing how many credits, messages, and users were active during a given billing period, along with a ranked list of the top ten heaviest users. It's a behind-the-scenes script for employees, not something you would see or interact with; if you were to look in the system today, you'd find this new option already available for anyone with the right access.

ai.title: Skip file reads for Codebuff meta queries
ai.summary: checkNewFilesNecessary logic updated to return NO for queries about the Codebuff application itself (model, credits, checkpoints). System prompt augmented with Codebuff context via new systemIntro constant. Scope limited to backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts. Prevents unnecessary file scanning when users ask agent meta-questions.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant about itself, like which model it uses, how many credits you've used, or how to undo a change, the system will no longer open up and read any extra project files to find the answer. Instead, it skips that file-scanning step entirely and just answers directly. This only affects those kinds of app-level questions, so asking it to write or edit your code still works exactly as before. The result is a slightly snappier response for meta questions and a bit less unnecessary work happening behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add local CI runner via act and refactor workflow
ai.summary: Introduced local CI execution support using `act` via new scripts `.github/act/bootstrap-act-config.sh` and `.github/act/run-local.sh`, exposed through the `bun act` command in `package.json`. The `ci.yml` workflow was refactored to merge `setup` and `build` jobs, removing the separate typecheck dependency chain and updating test globs. A new `.github/knowledge.md` file documents the pipeline structure and local runner configuration.

eli5.text: Developers can now run the project's automated checks (building, testing, etc.) directly on their own computer, instead of only running them on the cloud. A new tool was added that sets up a local simulation of the cloud system, and the team also simplified how the checking steps are organized so they run a bit more efficiently. Everything is ready to use today if you're a developer working on this project.

ai.title: Add Endless Auto-Updates troubleshooting
ai.summary: Added 'Endless Auto-Updates' section to troubleshooting docs. Addresses update loops caused by conflicting Node/npm installations between Homebrew and nvm. Includes diagnostic commands for checking paths and uninstalling Homebrew Node.

eli5.text: If Codebuff keeps restarting its update process over and over, it might be because your computer has two different versions of the Node software installed at the same time, which can happen if you used both Homebrew and nvm. The documentation now includes steps to check which version is being used and remove the one causing the conflict, so the update process can finish normally.

ai.title: Fix relative path resolution in getStartingDirectory
ai.summary: Updated `getStartingDirectory` to accept an optional path and resolve relative paths against the current working directory using a new `toAbsolutePath` helper. This ensures project directories specified via CLI arguments are correctly normalized to absolute paths before being set as the project root. Changes affect `npm-app/src/index.ts` and `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant and tell it which folder to work in using a quick relative reference like 'src' or '../project', it now correctly finds that folder instead of getting lost. Previously, typing a relative path could point the assistant to the wrong place; now it resolves that reference against the folder you're currently in, handling shortcuts like '..' and '.' properly, including on Windows. This affects anyone launching the tool from the command line with a folder argument. The fix is live today.

ai.title: Filter system instructions during context reset
ai.summary: Added `isSystemInstruction` checks in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/util/messages.ts` to exclude system instructions from message history and token trimming logic. This ensures system directives are stripped when resetting context or managing token limits, preventing them from interfering with user message processing. The change applies to the backend core, specifically affecting how `messageHistory` is filtered and how `trimMessagesToFitTokenLimit` handles string content.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to reset the conversation or make room for more messages, it now removes any internal system directives from the message history before processing new content. This prevents background instructions from cluttering or conflicting with your actual messages during trimming or reset. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were troubleshooting how the assistant handles long conversations, but behind the scenes the message history stays cleaner. The change is live now and only affects how internal message filtering works.

ai.title: cd logic checks pwd after command
ai.summary: Terminal command execution logic in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` was refactored to detect directory changes by checking the working directory (`pwd`) after the command completes, rather than intercepting `cd` commands beforehand. The `handleChangeDirectory` helper was removed, and the PTY command wrapper now injects `$(pwd)` into the completion signal to capture the final path. This ensures accurate state tracking for nested or aliased directory changes and simplifies the command parsing flow.

eli5.text: When you run a command that changes your current folder, the system now waits for the command to finish and then asks the shell where you ended up, instead of trying to guess your destination beforehand. This makes the assistant's sense of your location stay accurate even if the command uses a shortcut, changes folders more than once, or runs through a custom alias. If you looked, you would see the prompt no longer shows an extra "Command completed" line, and the final directory is reported directly in the result.

ai.title: Add nx reset to build script
ai.summary: The root `build` script in `package.json` now executes `nx reset` before `nx run-many`. This change ensures Nx's daemon and cache are cleared prior to building `common`, `packages/*`, `backend`, `npm-app`, and `web`, preventing stale cache artifacts from interfering with build integrity.

eli5.text: When you run a build of the project, it now clears out some temporary working files first before doing the actual build. This affects anyone running the build process on this codebase, like developers or automated systems assembling new versions. If you watched the build run, you'd see the step that wipes these temp files happening at the very start, before the list of components to build appears.

ai.title: CI setup-job action drops ENVLOCAL secret write
ai.summary: CI setup-job action drops ENV_LOCAL secret write, only appends CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true to .env.local. Removes redundant Get Credentials steps from build, test-frontend, test-backend jobs; test-frontend/test-backend now call ./.github/actions/setup-job directly. .github/knowledge.md documents act env flow: .env.act/.secrets.act supply vars, run-local.sh backs up/restores .env.local, CI writes only the flag. Composite action using value normalized to single quotes.

eli5.text: The automated test runner that checks your code for problems was simplified so it no longer writes sensitive setup data into a hidden configuration file called.env.local. Instead, it only adds a single flag (CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true) to that file, keeping the rest of the environment variables separate and managed through dedicated secret files. If you run tests locally with the `act` tool, your existing.env.local is now backed up and restored automatically, so you won't see your personal settings overwritten during test runs. This change is live today for all contributors using the CI pipeline.
